propertyJourney.intro: We check safety first. Then we help you preserve the facts and find a possible contact without deciding fault or coverage.
propertyJourney.privacy: Your answers are used only to guide you on this page. They are not stored or sent.
propertyJourney.title: Is there still an active danger, or are you unsure whether the property is safe to use?

danger.title: Move away from danger before continuing.
danger.body: Do not re-enter or restore gas, electricity, or water until local services or qualified experts say it is safe.
danger.emergency: Contact the appropriate local emergency, utility, or safety service. If you are in the EU, you can call 112 free of charge.

damage.title: What type of damage occurred?
damage.hint: Choose the closest description; you do not need to know the cause.

thirdParty.title: Is a neighbour, tenant, or another person involved?
thirdParty.hint: This only helps us suggest what to preserve. It does not decide fault or liability.

role.title: What is your role in relation to the property?
role.acting: I am acting for someone else with authority

countries.propertyTitle: Which country is the property in?
countries.propertyHint: Choose it yourself; we do not infer it from language, residence, or location.
countries.propertyLabel: Country where the property is located
countries.residenceTitle: Which country do you usually live in?
countries.residenceHint: This may be different from the country where the property is located.

evidence.title: Protect people and preserve the damage facts.
evidence.body: Take only safe steps. Do not delay urgent work or keep dangerous items only as evidence. This does not decide coverage, fault, repair method, or compensation.

items.safePhotos: Photos or video of affected areas and items only when it is safe.
items.inventory: A list of damaged or stolen items, dates, serial numbers, and relevant messages.
items.receipts: Receipts, estimates, and costs for emergency measures or temporary accommodation. Keep temporary damage-limitation work separate from permanent repair.

type.water: Where needed, contact a utility or qualified service; do not touch contaminated water or unsafe installations.
type.fire: Do not re-enter until local services or qualified experts say the area is safe.
type.storm: Limit further damage only when safe and keep receipts for temporary measures.
type.theft: The police may be an appropriate contact; keep the report reference if one is provided.
type.product: Stop using the item if it may be unsafe. Keep it only when safe and contact the seller, manufacturer, utility, or a qualified service when appropriate.
type.other: Preserve the date, place, and facts you already know and seek a qualified assessment when needed.
type.unsure: Seek a qualified inspection or guidance when the type or safety of the damage is unclear.

evidence.thirdParty: Preserve messages and contact facts without accepting or assigning fault.

role.owner: Notify the insurer or property manager when appropriate.
role.tenant: Notify the owner or property manager and the insurer when appropriate.
role.business: Notify the person responsible for the premises and the insurer when appropriate.
role.acting: The insurer, property owner or manager, and police are parallel possible contacts. This page does not prove authority.
role.unsure: The insurer, property owner or manager, and police are parallel possible contacts; choose according to the situation.

evidence.diasporaTitle: Is the property outside the country where you live?
evidence.diasporaBody: Country, policy, and contract rules need separate review. We do not assume why the countries differ or draw a legal conclusion.
evidence.handoff: A new Free Start intake begins now. None of these guidance answers carry over; you choose what to submit.
